$comment: The single source of truth for this repo's identity. Every launch phase (README, OSS scaffold, GitHub metadata) reads THIS file rather than re-deciding, so the name, pitch, license and topics say the same thing everywhere. Visual identity is deliberately absent: this project ships no logo, and an empty brand block is the honest record of that decision rather than an oversight.
name: lath
description: A task runner whose definitions are typed Go: exported functions are the commands, pipelines are values, and a deploy runs identically on a laptop, over ssh, and in CI.

brand.$comment: No logo, wordmark or icon by decision. color is kept only because shields.io badges need a hex, and a badge palette is not a visual identity.

positioning.audience: Go teams deploying containerised services to their own servers, who write the deploy in CI YAML today
positioning.wedge: A deploy you cannot run on your laptop is a deploy you debug in production. lath makes the definition a Go program, so the same pipeline runs locally against Docker, over ssh, or in CI with nothing swapped but a Runner.
alternatives: CI YAML with embedded shell (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI)
differentiators: The definition is typed Go: a step reading state nothing produces fails validation before anything runs, not three minutes into a deploy
plan and dry-run describe or rehearse the whole pipeline without side effects
A step debugger pauses, inspects and replays individual steps of a real run
Local and remote differ by one field, the Runner, so a rehearsal exercises the real code path
Primitives are a plain Go library any program can import, with no framework dependency
